source.text: ጥበብ፡ መካነ፡ ኢረከበት፡ ኀበ፡ ትኅድር፡ ወ*ሀለወ፡ ማኅደራ፡ ውስተ፡ ሰማያት።
source.note: Selected negative place/dwelling relation and starred existence clause retained; no assigning agent is supplied.

transcription_uncertainties.detail: English says her dwelling was, not an unprinted passive assignment or a named assigning agent.

translation.text: Wisdom found no place where she could dwell, and her dwelling was in the heavens.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected negative says Wisdom found no place to dwell. The following existence clause says her dwelling was in the heavens; it does not name an assigning agent or explicitly say that God assigned it to her. The selected star on that existence verb is retained.

source.text: ወፅአት፡ ጥበብ፡ ከመ፡ ትኅድር፡ ውስተ፡ ውሉደ፡ ሰብእ፡ ወኢረከበት፡ ማኅደረ፡ ጥበብ፡ ውስተ፡ መካና፡ ገብአት፡ ወ*ተጸዐነት፡ ማእከለ፡ መላእክት።
source.note: Selected return to her place and starred seat/mount-derived verb retained; the source names no throne or vehicle.

transcription_uncertainties.detail: Actual1305–1306 reflexive/insidere range supports seating. Not normalized to unprintedተቀመጠት; no throne or vehicle added.

translation.text: Wisdom went out to dwell among humankind, but she found no dwelling place. Wisdom returned to her place and took her seat among the angels.[a]

footnotes.text: The starred verb can involve taking a seat or mounting; “took her seat” follows its seating sense. The source does not name a throne or a vehicle, and neither is added here.

source.text: ወዐመፅ፡ ወፅአት፡ እምመዛግብቲሃ፡ ዘኢፈቀደት፡ ረከበት፡ ወኀደረት፡ ውስቴቶሙ፡ ከመ፡ ዝናም፡ በበዳው፡ ወከመ፡ ጠል፡ በምድር፡ ጽምእት።
source.note: Selected negative desire verb has the feminine subject Injustice; both rain/dew comparisons and plural recipients are retained without moral harmonization.

transcription_uncertainties.detail: The negative finite desire form is feminine singular, not pluralፈቀዱ. Injustice is subject of not wanting and finding. Englishthose is supplied from later pluralthem, not a subject reversal.

translation.text: Injustice went out from her storehouses. She found those she had not wanted and dwelt among them, like rain in a wilderness and like dew on thirsty earth.[a]

footnotes.text: Her and she follow the selected feminine verbs. In ዘኢፈቀደት, Injustice is the subject of did not want; this is not those who did not want her. Wanted retains the wishing/desire sense, not a substituted seek verb. Those follows the later plural among them. Rain in a wilderness and dew on thirsty earth remain the selected comparisons; no moral or geographic correction is supplied.
